headline: Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia along with Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav jointly chair investor and strategic roundtables in Mumbai; Discussions focus on strengthening India’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) and unlocking investment opportunities
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia along with Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav jointly chair investor and strategic roundtables in Mumbai; Discussions focus on strengthening India’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) and unlocking investment opportunities

TMZ will strengthen India’s position on the global telecom manufacturing map: Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

⁠India's first-of-its-kind Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior will advance Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat

DoT and COAI Organise Investor Roundtable and Strategic Roundtable on Capitalising India’s Telecom Decade and Promoting Telecom Manufacturing Zone

04 AUG 2026 10:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India in collaboration with the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), organised two important industry engagements in Mumbai today to advance the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. Both engagements were jointly chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh along with Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications. Both meetings mark a significant milestone in strengthening India's first-of-its-kind Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, which will advance Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector.

The first engagement was an Investor Roundtable focused on attracting investment and greater industry participation in the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior. Leading telecom and electronics companies, including Qualcomm, NTT DATA, Jio and other leading companies participated in the investor roundtable. Discussions focused on the investment potential of the TMZ, strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities, promoting exports, reducing import dependence and creating a globally competitive telecom and electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, said, “India must now transition from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. We must adopt a three-pronged strategy to achieve this transformation: increasing domestic value addition, creating intellectual property in India, and enabling Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured telecom products to reach every corner of the world.”

Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, said, “I would like to thank all the officials involved in this project. This important project is a joint step between Government of Madhya Pradesh and Union Government in the field of telecommunications. Madhya Pradesh has emerged as the top choice for set up industry especially related to manufacturing. With this in mind, I would like to invite you all to come and invest in Madhya Pradesh.”

Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, highlighted that “Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is a unique and first of its kind facility that has been envisioned jointly by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and Union Ministry of Communications. TMZ will create deep value addition driven by Intellectual Property within India helping India becoming a part in global supply chain in line with Hon’ble Prime Minister’s Vision of Made in India for India and the World.”

In the first roundtable held in Delhi, investment commitments worth ₹3,500 crore and 14,000 job opportunities were assured by the industry for the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

At the conclusion of the Investor Roundtable at Mumbai, participating companies committed investments worth more than ₹2,000 crore, expected to generate above 4,000 employment opportunities under the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ). In total, a commitment of more than ₹5500 crores of investments and above 18,000 employment opportunities were given by the industry towards the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ).

Eight global tech leaders, including Qualcomm, Ericsson and Nokia, along with leading IT companies such as TCS and Tech Mahindra, have expressed interest in considering the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) as an investment destination and establishing global service support and development centres in the zone.

All three private telecom service providers—Bharti Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea—appreciated the initiative and leadership of the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. They also affirmed that they would encourage their respective vendor ecosystems to explore opportunities for establishing supply chains and manufacturing facilities within the TMZ in Gwalior.

The second engagement was a Strategic Roundtable on “Capitalizing India’s Telecom Decade and Promoting Telecom Manufacturing Zone”. The strategic roundtable brought together key stakeholders from the telecom industry to deliberate on India’s next phase of telecom growth, strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and creating a globally competitive telecom ecosystem. Union Minister Sh. Jyotiraditya M. Scindia appreciated the role of investors in promoting Indian startup and Tech ecosystem. He invited the investors to India Mobile Congress being held from 7 to 10 October 2026 at Yashobhoomi New Delhi. The discussions also focused on identifying opportunities for greater industry participation and investment in the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

The roundtable was held in continuation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July 2026 for establishment of India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior. The MoU envisages a 170 acres plug-and-play industrial cluster offering world-class infrastructure and an integrated ecosystem for telecom and electronics manufacturing, research and development, innovation and allied activities. At the Strategic Roundtable, the participating stakeholders deliberated on further opportunities for investment, manufacturing and employment in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ).

The strategic roundtable reinforced the Government’s vision of moving India beyond being a telecom service provider towards becoming a global telecom product manufacturing and innovation hub. It also marked another important step towards translating the recently signed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) MoU into concrete investments, manufacturing and employment opportunities.

About Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior

The proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated 170-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster for telecom manufacturing, R&D and innovation, covering mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment and next-generation 5G/6G technologies. Under the recently signed MoU, the Central Government is providing 100% funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost along with various investor incentives.

The TMZ will be established through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) with 51% equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% from the Department of Telecommunications.

headline: Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

AIKCC leaders said during the meeting with Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh that Ethanol will increase farmers’ income and also secure the country’s energy

During the meeting with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, farmers said, “Ethanol is a new opportunity for farming”

“Farmers and the government should work together to break the wrong narrative on Ethanol”: AIKCC

“Not petrol, but Ethanol coming from the fields is the future of the country,” Farmer leaders from various states told Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Open discussion held on Ethanol and farmers’ income by farmer leaders from across the country at Krishi Bhavan, New Delhi

“The doors of Krishi Bhavan are open for farmers; farmers are like God”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

04 AUG 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

A delegation of the All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC) met Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday and categorically stated that Ethanol is a big opportunity for the farming sector, provided its policy is farmer-centric and the correct price of the crop reaches the farmer directly. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan carefully listened to all the suggestions of the farmer leaders and, while giving his guidance, assured that the Central Government will take the farmers’ views on Ethanol seriously. Shri Shivraj Singh said that farmers are like God for him and the doors of Krishi Bhavan are always open for farmers.

Farmer leaders from across the country speak openly on Ethanol at Krishi Bhavan

At Krishi Bhavan in New Delhi, a delegation of AIKCC met Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The delegation included farmer leaders from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and other parts of the country. The main focus of the meeting remained on Ethanol, farmers’ income, MSP (minimum support price), markets and the National Agriculture Policy. However, the farmers clearly said that they are in favour of Ethanol; they only want that the real benefit of this programme reaches the farmer and not only companies or middlemen.

What farmers said in favour of Ethanol

During the meeting, the farmer leaders made their stand on Ethanol clear and said that with Ethanol, the produce of the field will not remain limited only to the mandi (market), but will reach petrol pumps and the energy market. This will create a new and strong market for farmers. When Ethanol is made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstocks, farmers will get more buyers and the problem of crop spoilage or storage will reduce.

The farmers said that they are not against Ethanol but are fully in its support. However, it is necessary that proper prices of any crop, whether maize or sugarcane, reach the farmers. The farmer representatives said that they want an Ethanol policy to create a new path for farming and not become a new worry for them. They said they are with Ethanol, if Ethanol also is with them.

‘It is necessary to clear misunderstandings on Ethanol’ – Farmer leaders

During the meeting, several farmer leaders said that confusion is being spread on social media and some platforms in the name of Ethanol – sometimes by saying that it damages vehicles, sometimes by saying that it harms farmers. The farmers demanded that the Union Agriculture Ministry and farmer organisations together clearly explain which crops will benefit in what way from Ethanol and how a shift can be made from water-intensive crops towards drought-tolerant crops. They said that to reach the young generation, it is necessary to show the correct picture of Ethanol through reels, short videos and ground-level meetings.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened to suggestions and gave guidance

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened carefully to the farmers throughout and kept asking questions in between to understand the ground situation. He said that the thought process of the Central Government is clear – the benefit of the Ethanol programme should reach the entire chain, from the field to the fuel tank, but the largest share should go in the interest of the farmer. Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that Ethanol will strengthen the country’s energy security as well as the farmers’ pockets. Our emphasis is on ensuring that no crop and no state faces injustice.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan gave the assurance in the meeting that the policy will be reviewed to maintain the balance of prices and demand of maize, rice, sugarcane and other feedstocks. Decisions will be taken only from the point of view of farmer interest, especially the benefit of maize farmers. Through the scientific studies and technical reports available on Ethanol, the negative narrative will be answered, and fact-based dialogue will be carried forward together with the farmers.

Farmers’ views, Minister’s guidance – Message of partnership

At the end of the meeting, the representatives of AIKCC said that they will take this message to the villages that the confusion regarding Ethanol will be broken on the basis of facts and ground experience, and the process of making policy in the interest of farmers will be strengthened by working together with the government. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also gave a clear message that farmer organisations are not opponents of the government but partners in policy. He said that we have carefully listened to the farmers’ views on Ethanol; now our work is to create such a framework on the basis of these suggestions in which the farmer, the country and energy – all three become strong.

The AIKCC delegation included National President of AIKCC and former MP from Bharatiya Kisan Union (Mann) Shri Bhupinder Singh Mann, National Vice-President of AIKCC and President of National Association for Farmer Producer Organisations (NAFPO) Shri Binod Anand, National Vice-President of AIKCC Shri Gurusahib Singh Mann, National General Secretary of AIKCC and trainer of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Gunwat Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann and President of Kisan Union Mann (UP) Shri Ajay Anmol, Member of AIKCC and Vice-President of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Lalit Bahale Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann (Haryana) Shri Balraj Singh Sandhu, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Surjit Singh Mani Gurjar, Member of AIKCC and State Vice-President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Jugnu Rana, Member of AIKCC and State General Secretary of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Manphool Singh, Member of AIKCC and President of Vyamalan Kisan Sangathan (Tamil Nadu) Shri V. Manikkam, Member of AIKCC and President of Kisan Jagaran (Telangana) Shri Sugunakar Rao, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Chandigarh) Shri Balwant Singh Nadiyali, Member of AIKCC and Spokesperson of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Dinesh Sharma, Member of AIKCC and President of Malwa BKU Mann Shri Balveer Singh, and Member of AIKCC Shri Shivaraj Singh.

headline: Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone

Mumbai Investors’ Meet Attracts Fresh ₹2,000 Crore Commitments; Telecom Manufacturing Zone Set to Generate over 18,000 Employment Opportunities

India Advancing Towards a Global Standard, Best-in-Class Manufacturing Ecosystem Led By PM Modi: Scindia

04 AUG 2026 8:20PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai : 4 August 2026

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, along with Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, today co-chaired the second Investors’ Meet in Mumbai for India’s first and only Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, securing fresh investment commitments worth ₹2,000 crore for the initiative. The meeting witnessed participation from nearly 18 leading industry players from across the telecom ecosystem, with the latest commitments expected to generate close to 4,000 employment opportunities.

With the Mumbai commitments, the Telecom Manufacturing Zone has now attracted cumulative investment commitments worth ₹5,500 crore and is expected to create over 18,000 employment opportunities. This builds upon the ₹3,500 crore investment commitments and 14,000 jobs announced during the inaugural Investors’ Roundtable in New Delhi held last week, marking another significant milestone towards the TMZ’s vision of attracting over ₹10,000 crore in investments.

Addressing industry leaders, Minister Scindia said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has witnessed a transformational revolution in telecommunications and digitalisation over the last twelve years. He noted that India has evolved from a nation driven by telecom services into one preparing to become a global leader in telecom products and manufacturing.

Emphasising the vision of “Make in India, Make for the World” and “Local for Global”, the Minister said India must now transition from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. He outlined a three-pronged strategy to achieve this transformation: increasing domestic value addition, creating intellectual property in India, and enabling Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured telecom products to reach every corner of the world.

Drawing parallels with India’s remarkable success in mobile manufacturing and digital public infrastructure, Minister Scindia said that the same model can now be replicated in telecom manufacturing. He noted that India has transformed from importing the vast majority of its mobile phones to becoming one of the world’s largest mobile manufacturing hubs, while digital platforms such as UPI have demonstrated India’s ability to create globally scalable technology solutions. He expressed confidence that the TMZ in Gwalior would emerge as another global success story that countries around the world could look to replicate.

The Minister described the Telecom Manufacturing Zone as a first-of-its-kind initiative inspired by the success of Special Economic Zones but designed exclusively for the telecommunications sector. The integrated ecosystem will bring together the complete telecom value chain, including design, research and development, testing, manufacturing, components, semiconductors, optical fibre, telecom equipment and allied industries, supported by common plug-and-play testing infrastructure and world-class facilities.

Highlighting Gwalior’s strategic advantages, Minister Scindia said its central location, excellent connectivity, established industrial ecosystem, availability of plug-and-play infrastructure, strong talent pipeline from premier educational institutions, and competitive operating costs make it an ideal destination for telecom manufacturing investments. Highlighting Gwalior’s rapidly evolving infrastructure, Minister Scindia noted that enhanced connectivity is significantly strengthening the city’s investment proposition. He said that with the upcoming high-speed Agra-Gwalior Greenfield Expressway and improved highway connectivity to the NCR, travel between Delhi-NCR and Gwalior will be completed in less than 3 hours.

He invited companies across every telecom vertical to establish operations in the Zone, creating a complete end-to-end manufacturing ecosystem.

The Minister also praised Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Government of Madhya Pradesh for their proactive partnership in making the Telecom Manufacturing Zone a reality. He highlighted the State’s industry-friendly incentives, including land availability, capital support, employment-linked incentives, skill development assistance and logistics advantages, which together make the project globally competitive.

Reaffirming the Government’s long-term commitment, Minister Scindia announced that a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) comprising representatives from both the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh will jointly steer the implementation of the project. Calling it an unprecedented Centre-State partnership, he assured investors that both governments would work together continuously to resolve issues, facilitate investments and ensure the long-term success of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

The Investors’ Meet was attended by Secretary, Department of Telecommunications Amit Agarwal, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh Neeraj Mandloi, senior government officials, industry leaders and investors from across the telecommunications ecosystem.

Source - Department of Telecommunications / Edgar Coelho/ Priti Malandkar

headline: Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026

04 AUG 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

On 04.08.2026, Air India Flight AI2379, operated by an Airbus A320 aircraft (VT-EXO) from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a momentary altitude variation during flight. The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely at Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi.

The flight was carrying 137 passengers, including 3 infants, and 8 crew members (2 pilots and 6 cabin crew).

Immediately upon landing, medical teams attended to all passengers and crew as a precautionary measure. Eight passengers and four cabin crew members have been admitted to hospitals for detailed medical evaluation and treatment. All admitted passengers and crew members are stable and are being provided with adequate medical care and attention. The remaining passengers were provided the necessary assistance and support.

Hon’ble Minister of Civil Aviation personally visited Fortis Hospital, accompanied by the Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation and DG DGCA to enquire about the condition of the injured passengers and assure them of all necessary assistance. Senior officers of the Ministry have also visited Fortis and Medanta Hospitals and are closely coordinating with the hospital authorities and the airline to ensure the best possible medical care and all necessary support to the injured.

The aircraft has been moved to the hangar and the Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder have been secured for detailed examination.

DGCA has initiated a detailed investigation into the occurrence. The Ministry of Civil Aviation and DGCA are closely monitoring the situation. Passenger safety remains the highest priority, and all necessary measures are being taken.

(Release ID: 2294547)
